rows.speaker: العتبي
rows.claim: Al-Atabi says the Torah records God’s instruction to build the ark, take family and animal pairs aboard, and expect forty days and nights of rain that would destroy earthly creatures.
rows.anchor: قال العتبي : قرأت في التوراة أن الله تعالى أوحى إليه أن أصنع الفلك

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil counts seventy-two men and women together with Noah’s sons and their wives, totaling seventy-eight people, half male and half female.
rows.anchor: وعن مقاتل كانوا اثنين وسبعين رجلا وامرأة وأولاد نوح ونساؤهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says eighty men and women were aboard; one was Jurhum, and a village near Mosul was named the Village of the Eighty because they built it after disembarking.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما كان في سفينة نوح ثمانون رجلا وامرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishari reading: the arrival of God’s command marks the limit at which the servant is ordered to board the ark of the Sharia.
rows.anchor: حد البلاغة التي يكون العبد مأمورا بالركوب على سفينة الشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oven boiling over symbolizes the water of carnal desire surging from the body’s oven.
rows.anchor: يفور ماء الشهوة من تنور القالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ark is the Sharia, and its passengers carry every trait of the lower self together with its counterpart: lust/chastity, greed/contentment, stinginess/generosity, anger/forbearance, rancor/safety, enmity/love, pride/humility, and deliberation/hastiness.
rows.anchor: قلنا احمل فيها في سفينة الشريعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s family symbolizes the spirit’s qualities; the excluded one is the lower self, while believers with Noah signify the heart and secret, of which only a few qualities generally believe.
rows.anchor: وأهلك أي : واحمل معك أهلك صفات الروح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qualities left outside the Sharia’s ark drown in the flood of trials; this rebuts philosophers and libertines who think moral self-treatment can save them without revealed law.
rows.anchor: كل ما كان من هذه الصفات وأزواجها في معزل عن سفينة الشريعة فهو غريق في طوفان الفتن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Natural disposition cannot know how or how much to purify the self; prophets are divinely knowledgeable physicians who teach health from illness and medicine from disease, enabling adornment with Sharia ethics.
rows.anchor: الطبيعة لا تعلم كيفية الإصلاح والعلاج ولا مقدار تزكية النفس وتحليتها

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: Al-Kawashi parses “in God’s name is its running and mooring” with “running” as the subject, “in God’s name” as its predicate, and “mooring” coordinated; Noah invoked God at both launch and landing.
rows.anchor: بسم الله مجراها خبر ومبتدأ ومرساها عطف عليه

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: The reading of majrāhā with either a or u is a verbal noun from two synonymous forms, while marsāhā with u derives from the ship coming to rest.
rows.anchor: ومجراها ضما وفتحا مصدر أجريته وجريت به لغتان بمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s forgiveness of sins and mercy toward servants explain their rescue from this catastrophe.
rows.anchor: إن ربي لغفور للذنوب والخطايا رحيم لعباده ولهذا نجاكم من هذه الداهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their rescue was not earned by merit but came solely through God’s favor, forgiveness, and mercy, as Sunni doctrine maintains.
rows.anchor: نجاتهم ليست بسبب استحقاقهم لها بل بمحض فضل الله وغفرانه ورحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believing old woman asked Noah to tell her when to board, but he forgot while loading the ark; she later found that God had saved her safely inside her house without her seeing the flood.
rows.anchor: قد وقع وكان أمر الله مفعولا وتعجب من أمر العجوز فإن الله تعالى قد أنجاها في بيتها

rows.speaker: بعض أهل الكشف
rows.claim: Some people of spiritual unveiling identify the site of Bursa’s Great Mosque as the old woman’s house.
rows.anchor: قد صح عن بعض أهل الكشف أن موضع الجامع الكبير في بلدة بروسه كان بيتا للعجوز المذكورة

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The Mathnawi says perfected people can know and see a person from afar, even years before birth, in proportion to the polish of their inner perception.
rows.anchor: كاملان ازدور نامت بشنوند تا بقعرباد وبودت درروند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sharia’s ark saves from the tempests of the lower self and world; merely boarding by instinct or imitation, as hypocrites and Iblis did, gives no true rescue, which requires obeying the divine command.
rows.anchor: من ركب سفينة الشرع بالطبع وتقليد الآباء والاستاذين لم ينفعه للنجاة الحقيقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In God’s name” means the ark’s movement originates from God and its return is to God, as the verse says the final destination is to the Lord.
rows.anchor: يكون مجريها من الله ومرساها إلى الله كقوله : إن إلى ربك المنتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the ishari reading, God is forgiving to those saved by boarding the ark and merciful to those who board by command rather than instinct.
rows.anchor: بالنجاة لمن ركبها رحيم لمن ركبها بالأمر لا بالطبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successive guardians include two angels at right and left and two in front and behind, echoing the angels seated on either side who record deeds.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى : عن اليمين وعن الشمال قعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report lists ten angels per person: two front and back, one at the forehead who raises the humble and crushes the arrogant, two at the lips, one guarding the mouth from a snake, and two at the eyes; night angels descend alongside day angels, while Satan is present by day and his offspring by night.
rows.anchor: فهؤلاء عشرة أملاك على كل آدمي فتنزل ملائكة الليل على ملائكة النهار

rows.speaker: بعض الأئمة
rows.claim: Some imams say the angels who raise a person’s daily deeds are the same pair who remain with him throughout life.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الأئمة : إن قلت الملائكة التي ترفع عمل العبد في اليوم هم

rows.speaker: بعض الأئمة
rows.claim: When the person dies, the angels ask where to go; God sends them to his grave to glorify and praise Him and record those acts for the servant until resurrection.
rows.anchor: فإذا مات قالا يا رب قد قبضت عبدك فإلى أين نذهب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the guardians as the ruler’s bodyguards, censuring the heedless for trusting guards to protect them from God’s decree.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعقبات أعوان السلطان فهو توبيخ الغافل المتمادي في غروره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rational person knows that divine decrees and destined calamities cannot be guarded against.
rows.anchor: العاقل يعلم أن القضايا الإلهية والنوازل المقدرة مما لا يمكن التحفظ منه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Obedience and charity are said to protect a believer from punishment at death, in the grave, and at resurrection.
rows.anchor: ويقال للمؤمن طاعات وصدقات يحفظونه من عذاب الله عند الموت وفي القبر

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: A report from an early authority says a dying believer’s head, heart, and feet are found to contain Quran, fasting, and night prayer; because he guarded himself, God guards him.
rows.anchor: قال بعض السلف : إذ احتضر المؤمن يقال للملك : شم رأسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God changes a people’s well-being and blessing when they abandon gratitude and turn from good conditions to bad ones.
rows.anchor: إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم من العافية والنعمة حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم حتى يتركوا الشكر

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Hafez’s Persian verse says Qarun’s treasure still sinks in divine wrath and links this to the dervishes’ jealousy.
rows.anchor: كنج قارون كه فروميرود از قهر هنوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man became mute as punishment for filial impiety after his mother called him and he did not answer.
rows.anchor: وغير اللسان على رجل بسبب العقوق ، نادته والدته فلم يجبها فصار أخرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barsisa’s faith was changed after 220 years of uninterrupted worship because he failed to thank God for the blessing of Islam even for one day.
rows.anchor: وغير الإيمان على برصيصا بعد ما عبد الله مائتين وعشرين سنة

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Hafez’s couplet teaches that gratitude increases blessings while ingratitude removes them.
rows.anchor: شكر نعمت نعمتت افزون كند كفر نعمت از كفت بيرون كند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about God willing harm means destruction for the intended people, with no repelling it; the implied governor of “when” is the following assertion that it is not repelled.
rows.anchor: وهلاكا فلا مرد له فلا رد له ، والعامل في إذا ما دل عليه ، قوله فلا مرد له

rows.speaker: نحاة البصرة
rows.claim: Basran grammarians treat idhā primarily as a temporal adverb that can also condition a clause without losing its temporal sense; thus “when you rise, I rise” means my rising occurs at the time of yours.
rows.anchor: وإذا عند نحاة البصرة حقيقة في الظرف وقد تجيء للشرط من غير سقوط معنى الظرف

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: Kufan grammarians allow idhā to function as both time adverb and conditional particle, citing two poetic examples.
rows.anchor: وعند الكوفيين يجيء للظرف والشرط نحو وإذا يحاس الحيس يدعى جندب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No protector besides God can manage the affairs of people He wills to destroy or ward harm from them; al-Wālī is a divine name for the ruler who enforces decisions over others.
rows.anchor: {وما لهم} أي : لمن أراد تعالى إهلاكه من دونه سوى الله تعالى من وال ممن يلي أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This proves that opposing God’s will is impossible: He alone directs all things and none can revise His judgment.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن خلاف مراد الله محال فإنه المتفرد بتدبير الأشياء المنفذ للتدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lightning is the gleam from a cloud; the word barq describes something shining or flashing.
rows.anchor: الذي يلمع من السحاب من برق الشيء بريقا إذا لمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In fear and hope” can mean either intending fear or causing it through lightning strikes and ruined homes, and intending hope or inspiring expectation of blessing and relief.
rows.anchor: خوفا أي : إرادة خوف أو إخافة من الصاعقة وخراب البيوت وطمعا أي إرادة طمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain brings harm to travelers, people with stored dates or raisins, and those with leaky homes, but hope to residents, farmers, and orchard keepers; Egyptians rely on the Nile and may not benefit from rain.
rows.anchor: والمطر يكون لبعض الأشياء ضررا ولبعضها رحمة فيخاف مه المسافر ومن في خزينته التمر والزبيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flash also signifies that divine beauty contains majesty and divine majesty contains beauty; a flash of majesty gives the wayfarer fear and despair, while a flash of beauty gives hope and expectation.
rows.anchor: في باطن جمال الله تعالى جلالا وفي باطن جلاله جمالا وأسند الإراءة إلى ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates clouds anew, and “heavy” describes them as full of water.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أن السحاب يعدمه الله تعالى ثم يخلقه جديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators differ over whether rainwater descends from the sky into clouds or God creates it within the clouds before rain falls.
rows.anchor: واختلف في أن الماء ينزل من السماء إلى السحاب ، أو يخلقه الله في السحاب فيمطر

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh rejects the theory that earthly vapor rises and cools into rain: rainfall varies in size, spacing, and duration despite constant earth and sun, so a freely choosing agent must specify its forms.
rows.anchor: وفي حواشي ابن الشيخ : السحاب جسم مركب من أجزاء رطبة مائية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address “We sent you” literally and technically concerns Muhammad, the possessor of revelation and the prophetic call.
rows.anchor: عبارة الخطاب في أرسلناك للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فهو المرسل لغة واصطلاحا وصاحب الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its ishari implication extends to each spiritual heir who follows Muhammad’s way until the end of time: such heirs guide by inspiration and have inward spiritual influence, though they are not messengers in the technical sense.
rows.anchor: إشارته لكل واحد من ورثته الذين هم على مشربه إلى يوم القيامة بحسب كونه مظهرا لأرثه

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The saying that scholars of Muhammad’s community are like Israelite prophets grants them prophethood only in the sense of receiving reports from God through inspiration.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "علماء أمتي كأنبياء بني إسرائيل" فأثبت لهم النبوة بمعنى الإخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who receive blessings should thank the Benefactor through faith; disbelief and denial are among the worst traits, while faith and affirmation are among the best, and good belief has powerful effects.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله : {وهم يكفرون بالرحمان} إشارة إلى أن المنعم عليه يجب أن لا يكفر المنعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A band of robbers called themselves warriors when questioned by a lodge host; a woman used their handwashing water on her blind daughter as a blessing, and the girl awoke cured, illustrating the effect of good opinion.
rows.anchor: فسأل عنهم صاحب الرباط فاستحيوا منه وقالوا نحن الغزاة فهيأ لهم طعاما

rows.speaker: مشركو مكة
rows.claim: Meccan polytheists, including Abu Jahl and Abd Allah ibn Umayya, proposed that Muhammad move the mountains, widen the land with gardens and streams, and resurrect ancestors such as Qusayy so they could question them.
rows.anchor: روى إن نفرا من مشركي مكة معهم أبو جهل بن هشام وعبد الله بن أمية قالوا يا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After they proposed these signs, the verse beginning “If there were a Quran” was revealed with its conditional answer omitted, as the author says he will explain later.
rows.anchor: فلما اقترحوا عليه هذه الآيات نزل قوله : ولو أن الخ وجواب الشرط محذوف كما سيأتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian gloss explains moving mountains as transferring them from their places and driving them off the earth, and splitting the land as making rivers and springs.
rows.anchor: سيرت به الجبال التسيير بالفارسية (برفتن آوردن) أي نقلت من أماكنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was sent with signs, including the hand, staff, and other miracles proving his prophethood; “that” explicates an understood command to take his people from darknesses of error to the light of faith, knowledge, and certainty.
rows.anchor: ملتبسا بآياتنا يعني اليد والعصا وسائر معجزاته الدالة على صحة نبوته

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: Abu al-Su‘ud takes the signs as miracles shown to the Israelites and the deliverance as their post-Pharaoh passage from disbelief and ignorance to faith, monotheism, and the other commands.
rows.anchor: وقال المولى أبو السعود رحمه الله : الآيات معجزاته التي أظهرها لبني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers a reading in which the signs are miracles, not the Torah, and Moses’s “people” are the Copts—Pharaoh and his followers—because the Quran says Moses was sent to Pharaoh and his chiefs at the outset of his mission.
rows.anchor: ينادي بأعلى صوته على أن المراد بالآيات غير التوراة وبالقوم القبط وهم فرعون واتباعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was sent to all humanity, so his charge says “the people,” not “your people”; deliverance occurred through his mission, while the Copts never accepted Moses’s call although the Israelites did.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى في حقه [إبراهيم : 1-25]{لتخرج الناس} ولم يقل لتخرج قومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger begins by warning, as Noah said he was a clear warner; thus “remind them of God’s days” means warning of past nations’ punishments so the people fear and believe.
rows.anchor: كما قال نوح عليه السلام في أول الأمر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression “days of the Arabs” refers to their major battles and wars, such as Hunayn and Badr.
rows.anchor: وأيام العرب ملاحمها وحروبها كيوم حنين ويوم بدر وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The town was lifted close to heaven on Gabriel’s wing and then overturned upon its people, leaving it inverted.
rows.anchor: بأن رفعناها إلى قريب من السماء على جناح جبريل ثم قلبناها عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the grammar, “its upper part” is the first object of “We made” and “its lower part” the second; this order intensifies the horror compared with the reverse.
rows.anchor: وقوله عاليها مفعول أول لجعلنا وسافلها مفعول ثان له وهو أدخل في الهول والفظاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stones rained down during the upheaval before the town’s inversion was complete.
rows.anchor: وأمطرنا عليهم في تضاعيف ذلك قبل تمام الانقلاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qamus defines sijjil as clodlike stones or a Persian-derived term; other explanations say the stones were baked in Hell, inscribed with the people’s names, or came from the decree recording their punishment, equating sijjil with sijjin.
rows.anchor: قال في القاموس السجيل كسكيت حجارة كالمدر معرب (سنك كل) أو كان طبخت بنار جهنم

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari calls the explanation of sijjil as sijjin, a record of punishment, the clearest of the reported definitions.
rows.anchor: قال الأزهري هذا أحسن ما مر عندي وأبينها

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: Al-Kawashi says the stones also fell on those who were away from the affected lands.
rows.anchor: وفي "الكواشي" : وأمطرنا على شذاذهم ، أي : على من غاب عن تلك البلاد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs include Lot’s people’s attempted assault on Abraham’s guests, the overturning of the city, and stones falling on the city and its absentees.
rows.anchor: أي فيما ذكر من القصة من تعرض قوم لوط لضيف إبراهيم طمعا فيهم وقلب المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “perceptive” are reflective people who scrutinize a thing’s marks until they recognize its reality and inward nature; the term connotes physiognomic insight.
rows.anchor: أي : المتفكرين المتفرسين الذين يبسطون في نظرهم حتى يعرفوا حقيقة الشيء وباطنه بسمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruined towns remain beside a stable, traveled route between Mecca and Syria, so Quraysh should take warning when journeying to Syria because their traces have not disappeared.
rows.anchor: لبسبيل مقيم أي طريق ثابت يسلكه الناس ويرون آثار تلك البلاد بين مكة والشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The visible ruins are a great sign for believers, who know punishment followed wrongdoing; others explain them as chance or astrological configurations. The singular “sign” refers to the remaining traces alone, unlike the whole story previously described.
rows.anchor: لآية عظيمة للمؤمنين بالله ورسوله فإنهم الذين يعرفون أن ما حاق بهم من العذاب

rows.speaker: برهان القرآن
rows.claim: Burhan al-Quran explains that plural “signs” denotes multiple proofs, whereas singular “sign” marks the oneness of what is signified; the singular suits believers who affirm God’s unity.
rows.anchor: وقال في برهان القرآن : ما جاء في القرآن من الآيات فلجمع الدلائل ، وما جاء من الآية

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A prophetic report says earlier nations had inspired people who received impressions from the higher realm and spoke correctly by intuition; this is a high rank among saints, and Umar is the foremost example in this community, with the conditional wording emphasizing his distinction rather than expressing doubt.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : إن كان فيما مضى قلبكم من الأمم محدثون المحدث بفتح الدال المشددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet says it is poor manners to see oneself as great in a gathering where the sun itself is counted as a mote.
rows.anchor: در محفلي كه خورشيد اندر شمار ذره است خودرا بزرك ديدن شرط أدب نباشد

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: After the servant returns to his resting place through divine attraction, God creates in him what he had not known before: reception of the effusion of God’s light without intermediary.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {ويخلق} فيكم بعد رجوعكم بالجذبة إلى مستقركم {ما لا تعلمون} قبل الرجوع إليه

rows.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi says the Prophet left succession unmentioned because a member of the community can receive directly from God, be God’s inward deputy and the Messenger’s outward deputy, and share the source from which angels and prophets receive; the wali remains below prophethood and does not add outward rulings.
rows.anchor: قال حضرة الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره الاطهر سكت النبي عليه السلام عن الاستخلاف إذ في أمته من يأخذ الأمر عن ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is a road with a clear destination that its traveler follows without deviation; God, through mercy and a firm promise rather than obligation, makes it known by proofs, messengers, and revealed books so people may reach tawhid.
rows.anchor: القصد مصدر بمعنى الفاعل يقال سبيل قصد وقاصد أي : مستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “some of it” is parsed as a nominative subject, either substantivized or with an omitted noun meaning part of the path; the pronoun may be feminine because سبيل is used with either gender.
rows.anchor: {ومنها} في محل الرفع على الابتداء إما باعتبار مضمونه وإما بتقدير الموصوف

rows.speaker: ابن الكمال
rows.claim: Ibn al-Kamal distinguishes the terms: a path may be any traveled route, a sabil is habitually traveled, and a sirat is a straight, untwisted sabil, the narrowest category.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الكمال : الفرق بين الطريق والصراط والسبيل أنها متساوية في التذكير والتأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God wished to guide everyone with an invariably effective guidance to tawhid, He could; He did not because compulsion would remove the partial choice on which moral responsibility, reward, and punishment depend.
rows.anchor: ولو شاء الله أن يهديكم إلى ما ذكر من التوحيد هداية موصلة إليه البتة

rows.speaker: أبو الليث
rows.claim: Abu al-Layth says God would have guided all creatures if He knew them all to be fit for tawhid.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الليث في "تفسيره" : لو علم الله أن الخلق كلهم أهل للتوحيد لهداهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author develops Abu al-Layth’s point through fixed essences: divine knowledge follows what each essence gives it, so God wills guidance for those whose nature is faith and obedience, while willing otherwise for those whose preparedness differs; changing that would imply change in God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: هو معنى لطيف مبني على أن العلم تابع للمعلوم فلا يظهر من الأحوال إلا ما أعطته الأعيان إلى العلم الإلهي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith says the Messenger has no independent power over guidance and Satan has none over misguidance; if either power belonged to them, all people would believe or all would be led astray, but God guides or misguides as He wills.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "إنما أنا رسول وليس إلي شيء من الهداية ولو كانت الهداية إلي لآمن كل

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Hafez’s poems urge the hearer not to reproach himself for sin or piety, since people follow the course assigned to them and have no independent choice.
rows.anchor:
قال الحافظ :
13
مكن بشم حقارت ملامت من مست كه نيست معصيت وزهد بي مشيت او

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He concludes by urging readers to leave disputation and reject Mu‘tazilite argument: contentment and submission bring acceptance, while opposition leads to the wrath of the beloved.
rows.anchor: فعليك بترك القيل والقال ورفض الاعتزال والجدال فإن الرضى والتسليم سبب القبول
